newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Gold - Canada casts eye on local miners.
newsitem.headline: Australia Gold - Canada casts eye on local miners.

text.p: Canadian investors are looking to beef up interests in Australian gold mining companies.

Speculation on a takeover bid by Toronto-based Barrick Gold Corp for Great Central Mines NL, which mines the Bronzewing and Jundee deposits of Western Australia's Yandal belt is a recent indication of a mounted effort by Canadian groups to target Australia, investment brokers and miners said.
Great Central chairman Joe Gutnick has refused to deny or confirm the basis for the speculation.
Still, there is little doubt that Canadian companies are eyeing Australian miners and that they are receiving a warm reception.
Depressed gold prices are making it more difficult to fund exploration and expansion at home, which is encouraging more miners to look abroad for financing.

Bullion has rebounded to about US$324 an ounce from 12-year lows of around $313 an ounce in July following an announcement by the Reserve Bank of Australia that it had sold two-thirds of its gold reserves in favour of foreign currency backed securities.
Within four days of the announcement, the Australian Stock Exchange gold index, a measure of the health of Australian gold companies, tumbled 16 percent.
Representatives of the Vancouver Stock Exchange are currently on an Australian roadshow after meeting with junior mining houses in Kalgoorlie at the annual Diggers and Dealers conference this week.
"For many companies, a listing in Canada is a win-win situation," said one Vancouver Stock Exchange representative.
"Many junior mining companies just can't raise the money in Australia," he said.
The ability of Australian miners to turn to offshore markets for capital underscores the growing sophistication of the local industry.
Adelaide-based Normandy Mining Ltd, one of Australia's largest gold miners, plans a listing on the Toronto Stock Exchange later this year.

"Mining is a global business," said Warren Gilman, vice-chairman of CIBC Wood Gundy Australia Holdings Pty Ltd, which last week said it had agreed to acquire Eyres Reed Ltd, a Perth-based brokerage specialising in resource companies.
Gilman said Australian gold miners would benefit from the international exposure and capital raising prowess of CIBC, Canada's second largest merchant bank.
For its part, CIBC gains a presence on the ground in Australia.
Gilman said there was no "commodity-specific" focus to CIBC's plans in Australia. But it is clear gold will play a key role, given Western Australia's dominance of gold production within Australia.
Western Australia produces about 75 percent of Australia's annual gold yield of nearly 300 tonnes.
Low gold prices may have taken the shine off some gold mining companies, but in others it's created bargains.
"It's times like these that make great shopping opportunities," said David Reed, chairman of Eyres Reed.
-- Perth Bureau 618 9261-7111
